text: Although aerobic exercise can positively affect muscle mass in the untrained, compelling evidence indicates that it is suboptimal for promoting muscle growth in physically active people. For those who are sedentary, virtually any stimulus challenges the neuromuscular system and thus leads to an accretion of muscle proteins. Adaptations in these early stages are therefore more indicative of the novelty of the exercise bout as opposed to an increased potential for chronic adaptation. On the other hand, well-trained people have already adapted to lower-level stresses, and it therefore remains highly doubtful that aerobic training would provide enough stimulus for further muscular adaptation.
